investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T02:01–02:08Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for ~142–146 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never assigned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. The four remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules and cannot be used as fallback. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately Unschedulable. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint at the infrastructure layer, not an eval infrastructure misconfiguration. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this scheduling blockage.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector') with latencyMs=148051, confirming the scheduling failure is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same Unschedulable message with latencyMs=152643, confirming all three independent remote-agent pod requests hit the same capacity wall.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the agent VM never being created because the pod never scheduled.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial progress was recorded, confirming the failure occurred before any agent lifecycle step completed.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes also lack vm capacity, the effective schedulable pool is zero.

Tertiary — resource quota or LimitRange at the namespace or org level capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below what the eval probe requires, causing requests to be rejected even if raw node capacity exists.

Lower probability — a recent cluster node drain, node failure, or scale-down event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously sufficient count to the current 2, without a corresponding capacity increase on remaining nodes.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T02:03–02:08Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node cluster has zero available nodes capable of scheduling a new kata.peerpods.io/vm pod — 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the check produced no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), violating the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With no preemption victims available and preemption not helpful on any node, every new remote agent pod is left Unschedulable. This caused the eval runner to time out waiting for the agent pod to reach a ready state (~145 s), preventing any evidence from being collected and triggering a contract validation failure for all required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-07-17T02:03–02:08Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VMs: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner never received any response, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent workload has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule new agent pods. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept the pod: the 2 nodes that carry the kata peer-pod VM resource were already fully allocated, and the 4 remaining nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure that prevented the eval's createAgent call from ever producing a running VM, so no evidence was collected and the expected-output contract was violated in full. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production Kubernetes cluster; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Tertiary — cluster scaling not triggered or too slow: the cluster may rely on a node autoscaler for kata peer-pod capacity that did not provision a new node within the eval's timeout window (~142–152 s across all three checks).

Quaternary — eval concurrency: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create at 02:03, remote-agent-state at 02:06, remote-agent-runtime at 02:06) ran in close succession and may have competed for the same limited VM slots, compounding exhaustion.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T02:01–02:08Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for ~142–146 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never assigned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that carry that resource. The four remaining nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules and cannot be used as fallback. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request is immediately Unschedulable. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint at the infrastructure layer, not an eval infrastructure misconfiguration. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this scheduling blockage.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=148006, status=fail — pod was stuck unscheduled for 142s before the eval gave up, well within the outageLatencyMs=360000 threshold, confirming the pod never progressed past scheduling.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector') with latencyMs=148051, confirming the scheduling failure is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same Unschedulable message with latencyMs=152643, confirming all three independent remote-agent pod requests hit the same capacity wall.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the agent VM never being created because the pod never scheduled.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial progress was recorded, confirming the failure occurred before any agent lifecycle step completed.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which submits the pod; the scheduler rejection prevents this call from returning a VM-backed agent, so no evidence is written.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated because the pod never reached a running state.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a specific node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool. If those 2 nodes also lack vm capacity, the effective schedulable pool is zero.

Tertiary — resource quota or LimitRange at the namespace or org level capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below what the eval probe requires, causing requests to be rejected even if raw node capacity exists.

Lower probability — a recent cluster node drain, node failure, or scale-down event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously sufficient count to the current 2, without a corresponding capacity increase on remaining nodes.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots before this eval run began, leaving no capacity for new agent pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 non-kata nodes are excluded by the pod spec's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If those 2 nodes are undersized for the expected eval concurrency, exhaustion will recur.

Tertiary — cluster scaling not triggered or too slow: the cluster may rely on a node autoscaler for kata peer-pod capacity that did not provision a new node within the eval's timeout window (~142–152 s across all three checks).

Quaternary — eval concurrency: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create at 02:03, remote-agent-state at 02:06, remote-agent-runtime at 02:06) ran in close succession and may have competed for the same limited VM slots, compounding exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod affinity/selector rules were recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes would shift the primary cause from capacity exhaustion to a configuration regression.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state at the same timestamp would disprove the shared-capacity-exhaustion explanation and suggest the failure is isolated to the runtime check's pod spec.
